question: Pour a glass of water into the sea and let it mix through every ocean. Then scoop up a glass. How many of your molecules come back?
answer: About 1,500. A 250 ml glass holds about 8.4 trillion trillion molecules of water, and all the oceans hold about 5.3 billion trillion glasses. Divide one by the other and every glass of sea carries roughly 1,570 of yours, once the mixing is done, which takes about a thousand years.
move: When numbers get huge, count the zeros instead of trusting the feeling.
ask: Which huge number did I last judge by feel instead of by its zeros?

scene.unit: of your molecules in every glass
scene.compare: Every glass of sea holds some of yours

options.label: None
options.note: Not none. There are more molecules in a glass than glasses in all the seas.

options.label: About 1
options.note: Three zeros short. A glass holds more molecules than the seas hold glasses.

options.label: About 1,000
options.note: Right order. Every glass of sea on Earth holds some of your water.

options.label: A million
options.note: Three zeros too many. The seas dilute your glass five billion trillion times.

reference: NOAA National Ocean Service, 'How much water is in the ocean?' (about 1.335 billion cubic km). 250 ml of water is 13.9 mol; 13.9 × 6.022×10²³ ≈ 8.4×10²⁴ molecules; 1.335×10²¹ litres ÷ 0.25 ≈ 5.3×10²¹ glasses.

question: In 2023 Reddit priced its API at $0.24 per 1,000 requests. What would a year have cost Apollo, one popular Reddit app?
answer: About $20 million. Apollo's developer, Christian Selig, said the app had made 7 billion requests in a month: about $1.7 million a month at that price, or roughly $2.50 per user. He could not pay it, and Apollo shut down on 30 June 2023.
move: Multiply a tiny unit price by the real volume before calling it cheap.
ask: Which small per-use price am I paying without ever multiplying it out?

options.note: Two zeros short. A fortieth of a cent a tap adds up over 7 billion taps a month.

options.label: $2 million
options.note: One zero short. That was roughly one month's bill, not a year's.

options.label: $20 million
options.note: Right. About $1.7 million a month, $20 million a year, for one app.

options.label: $200 million
options.note: One zero too many. But $20 million was already far out of reach.

reference: Christian Selig, 'Had a call with Reddit to discuss pricing. Bad news for third-party apps, their announced pricing is close to Twitter's', r/apolloapp, 31 May 2023: $12,000 per 50 million requests, 7 billion requests last month, about $1.7 million a month or $20 million a year.

question: In April 2012 Facebook agreed to buy Instagram for about $1 billion. How many people worked at Instagram that day?
answer: Thirteen. Instagram had more than 30 million users and no revenue, run by a dozen-odd people on rented cloud servers. Software lets a tiny team serve millions, so a company's head count says little about what it is worth.
move: Head count measures cost, not value; software broke the link between them.
ask: Where am I judging how big something is by how many people it takes?

scene.compare: Over 2 million users for each of them

options.label: About 10
options.note: Right. Thirteen people, over 30 million users, one billion dollars.

options.label: About 100
options.note: One zero too many. Thirteen people ran it, on rented servers.

options.label: About 1,000
options.note: Two zeros too many. The whole company fitted in one small office.

options.label: About 10,000
options.note: Three zeros too many. Facebook itself had only about 3,000 staff.

reference: Evelyn M. Rusli, 'Facebook Buys Instagram for $1 Billion', The New York Times DealBook, 9 April 2012 (13 employees, more than 30 million users); Facebook Form S-1, 2012 (3,200 employees at 31 March 2012).
